classification.difficultyReason: Apply successive leading-term division and subtraction to cubic polynomials, retaining a constant remainder.

content.prompt: Use the division algorithm to divide $P(x)$ by $D(x)$. Find the quotient and the remainder.

answer.worked:
Divide successive leading terms and subtract the corresponding multiples of $x-1$.
$$\begin{align*}6x^3\div x&=6x^2\\(6x^3+7x^2-15x+4)-6x^2(x-1)&=13x^2-15x+4\\13x^2\div x&=13x\\(13x^2-15x+4)-13x(x-1)&=-2x+4\\-2x\div x&=-2\\(-2x+4)-(-2)(x-1)&=2\end{align*}$$
Thus $Q(x)=6x^2+13x-2$ and $R(x)=2$.
$$P(x)=(x-1)(6x^2+13x-2)+2.$$

Divide successive leading terms and subtract the corresponding multiples of $x+1$.
$$\begin{align*}2x^3\div x&=2x^2\\(2x^3-3x^2+5x+3)-2x^2(x+1)&=-5x^2+5x+3\\-5x^2\div x&=-5x\\(-5x^2+5x+3)-(-5x)(x+1)&=10x+3\\10x\div x&=10\\(10x+3)-10(x+1)&=-7\end{align*}$$
Thus $Q(x)=2x^2-5x+10$ and $R(x)=-7$.
$$P(x)=(x+1)(2x^2-5x+10)-7.$$

Divide successive leading terms and subtract the corresponding multiples of $x-3$.
$$\begin{align*}x^3\div x&=x^2\\(x^3-7x^2+6x+1)-x^2(x-3)&=-4x^2+6x+1\\-4x^2\div x&=-4x\\(-4x^2+6x+1)-(-4x)(x-3)&=-6x+1\\-6x\div x&=-6\\(-6x+1)-(-6)(x-3)&=-17\end{align*}$$
Thus $Q(x)=x^2-4x-6$ and $R(x)=-17$.
$$P(x)=(x-3)(x^2-4x-6)-17.$$

Divide successive leading terms and subtract the corresponding multiples of $x-2$.
$$\begin{align*}x^3\div x&=x^2\\(x^3-2x^2+3x+1)-x^2(x-2)&=3x+1\\3x\div x&=3\\(3x+1)-3(x-2)&=7\end{align*}$$
The coefficient of $x$ in the quotient is zero. Thus $Q(x)=x^2+3$ and $R(x)=7$.
$$P(x)=(x-2)(x^2+3)+7.$$
